passage1.text: Online classes began to be popularized just a few decades ago. They are advertised as a way for adults to finish their education and students to learn the material at their own pace ——it is far more compatible for people with busy schedules. 2022 年 6 月英语四级真题 第一套 页码 7 But after being enrolled in an online course last fall semester, I came to realize online classes were merely a means to fulfil course requirements. First of all, students lack the desire to learn, and they simply complete their assignments to receive credit for a passing grade rather than genuinely engage with the course material. As online courses tend to have more than 100 students, most of the assignments are short and simple. They are not designed for students to interact with the material in depth but designed to be graded easily to accommodate such a large number of students. Perhaps the biggest disadvantage of taking an online class is the absence of face-to-face interaction between the teacher and their students. Live sessions are infrequent and are often scheduled during the middle of the day when students have to attend other classes or work. The office hours of the professor may also be during inconvenient times for many students as well. Most interaction with the professor has to be through email which is often impersonal. It is nearly impossible for students to build a relationship with their professor. There is also little interaction amongst students. It can be harder for students to create study groups and form relationships with their peers. Online classes also require either a computer or laptop and a reliable internet connection. Not all students have access to these types of resources, whether it is for financial or other reasons, and some students can be put at a disadvantage. Offering online classes certainly helps students who would otherwise not be able to attend classroom sessions. However, they fail to provide a genuine education with an emphasis on convenience rather than critical thinking. We need restructured online classes in which students can have a learning experience that will actually provide quality education.

passage2.text: In the age of the internet, there's no such thing as a private debate. But is that bad for science? Some scientists have had concerns. When debates in any sector move beyond the halls of universities and government agencies, there's potential for information to be used incorrectly, leading to public confusion; yet, open debate can also promote communication between the scientific community and the public. Recent open debates on scientific research, health, and policy have aroused greater public attention and encouraged more diverse voices. If this trend spurs scientists to agree more quickly about the best solutions to our problems-and at the same time helps the public observe the process of scientific discourse more clearly- then this is good for everyone, including scientists. A recent debate published in The New York Times discussed the question of how quickly medicine should be developed and produced. Issues such as safety of the product and perception of the public were examined and considered. But some experts worried that such public speculation might lead people to believe that disagreement about the details meant a lack of adequate scientific consensus over the safety and efficiency of modern-day medicine. The anxiety seems misplaced. Gone are the days of going to a conference and debating scientific issues, and that's good because those gatherings were not diverse enough and excluded many important voices. These days, the public can access debates about science regardless of where they take place. For many scientists, public debate is a new frontier and it may feel like a place with few restraints or rules? but rather than avoiding such conversations, let the debates be transparent and vigorous, wherever they are held. If the public is to understand that science is an honorably self-correcting process, the idea that science is a fixed set of facts in a textbook needs to be dismissed. With the validity of science coming under attack, there's a need for scientific debates to be perceived as open and true to life. Let everyone see the noisy, messy deliberations that advance science and lead to decisions that benefit us all. 2022 年 6 月英语四级真题 第一套 页码 9

paragraphs.A: On paper, the job seemed perfect for me: The position was completely in line with my degree, the duties and responsibilities were compatible with my interests, and the office maintained a well-stocked kitchen that would satisfy my every snack desire.
paragraphs.B: Sounds like my dream job, right? There was only one small problem: I simply didn't get along with the company culture. They favored a more rigid, closed-door, corporate atmosphere, while I would have preferred something more collaborative and open. They were complete clock watchers, while I would have liked a more flexible schedule. To put it plainly, we just weren‘t on the same page.
paragraphs.C: When it comes to looking for a new job, you already know that a big part of the interview process involves the company evaluating whether or not you're a good fit for their open role. But, it's important to keep in mind that the employer isn't the only one who needs to identify a good match- you should be looking for that same exact thing. Company culture can have a big impact on how you feel about your work, so you want to make sure you sign an offer letter with an organization you're truly excited about.
paragraphs.D: However, figuring out what a company is like before you actually work there can be a bit of a challenge. Luckily, there are a few things you can do to determine whether or not a company is a good fit for you- before you ever sign your name on that dotted line.
paragraphs.E: First of all, know what you want. It's hard to make any decisions when you don't really know what you're looking for. So before you can determine whether you and a specific company would be compatible together, it's important to have a solid handle on what exactly you want from your employer. Many of us have an easier time identifying the things that we absolutely don't want. If those are the only things you can think of, don't 2022 年 6 月英语四级真题 第一套 页码 5 worry! That's still a good place to start.
paragraphs.F: Start by writing down the things you didn't like about previous employers, as well as the parts you really valued. There‘s no wrong answer here 一 so from big things to small details, write them all down on your list. This will help you immediately identify what you're looking for in an organization, as well as the things you're trying to stay far, far away from.
paragraphs.G: Make sure to do your research. Now comes the part when you put on your detective hat and do a little digging. The Internet will be your best friend when you're trying to familiarize yourself with a company's culture before ever walking through their office doors. And where exactly should you look for these culture clues? Start with the most obvious place first: the company's website. Read through their copy and blog. Do they use formal, direct language? Or is it casual, conversational, and maybe even a little humorous? This can be a big indicator of what sort of atmosphere the company is trying to cultivate.
paragraphs.H: Next, turn your attention toward their social media outlets. Are they sharing photos of their team's Thursday afternoon barbeque or Halloween costume contest? Or are their social media accounts strictly reserved for company-related announcements and product launches?
paragraphs.I: An industry review website like Glassdoor is another spot to check in order to find some insider information about what you can expect about a company. However, remember to take the reviews you read with a grain of salt-many of them are written by scorned (被鄙视的)employees.
paragraphs.J: Finally, you can never fail with personal connections. Send a quick message to a current or previous company employee on Linkedln or by email and ask if they would be willing to have a quick conversation with you about the organization in general. If you get a yes to your request for a chat, you‘ll be armed with some pretty powerful and helpful information heading into your interview!
paragraphs.K: Learn more by asking questions. You know that part at the end of a job interview when the hiring manager asks if you have any questions, and you just stare across the table blankly with your mouth hanging open? That's the perfect opportunity to speak up and get your burning company culture questions answered! So yes, you can definitely ask your interviewer about what it's like to work for that particular organization. Simple questions like, “What three words would you use to describe the culture here?” or “What's your favorite part about working for this company?can reveal a lot about what it's really like behind closed doors.
paragraphs.L: Prioritize your values. What does my dream company culture look like? Well, I could come and go as I please, as long as I was getting the work done. My boss would genuinely listen to and value all of my ideas arid suggestions. My co-workers would all be friendly with one another, without ever falling into the office gossip trap. The kitchen would have endless options of pizza and cookies. Oh, and they'd give me two months of paid vacation with a very generous salary. 2022 年 6 月英语四级真题 第一套 页码 6 M) What are my chances of finding all of those things with one employer? Slim to none—— believe me, I've looked. This is why it's so important to know which aspects of a company's culture you value most. Is it an open communication style or a flexible schedule? Focus on the top spots on your priority list, and ensure a potential employer at least checks those boxes. Unfortunately, this is reality, you can’t have everything you want but a few are certainly achievable. But you should also look at the process through a similar lens. You may not be the one conducting the actual interview, but you're still trying to determine whether or not the company is a good fit for you. questions.script:
A new study finds that beverages containing added sugar might be harmful.
In the study, researchers analyzed information from over 80,000 women and 37,000 men. Participants worked in the health profession. They were followed for approximately three decades. They completed surveys about their diet every four years. They also answered questions about sleep and exercise and health every two years.
The more beverages containing added sugar that people drank, the greater their risk of death was during the study period.
These beverages included soda, energy drinks and sports drinks. Beverages like pure fruit juice which are sweet but do not contain added sugar were not part of the study.
The findings held even after the researchers considered other factors that could affect people's health. These factors included lack of exercise and not eating enough vegetables. They also included consuming too much meat.
The scientists say that their results support limiting beverages with added sugar. They argue we should replace them with other drinks, with water being the best choice. However, the researchers admit this is simply their recommendation. The study found only an association: It did not prove that drinks with added sugar cause early death.

questions.script:
German police appealed Friday for information about the possible owners of two 17th-century oil paintings.
Police said a 64-year-old man found the paintings in a garbage pile at a highway rest stop last month. He later handed them in to the Cologne police.
An initial assessment by an art expert concluded the two framed paintings were originals, police said.
One is a landscape painted by the Italian artist Pietro Bellotti dating to 1665. The other is a painting of a boy by the 17th-century Dutch artist Samuel van Hoogstraten, date unknown. Their combined worth is estimated to be around one million euros.
Authorities have not yet confirmed what will happen if the rightful owner is not found. Nevertheless, it is speculated that they could either be handed over to the National Art Museum of Cologne or sold to the public by the local government.

questions.script:
A four-year-old girl has walked eight kilometers through a snowy forest to seek help for her sick grandmother who later died of a heart attack. The young girl braved the threat of bears, wolves and temperatures far below freezing. She made the journey through a remote region in Siberia after waking up to find her grandmother motionless.
Named locally as Karla, she lives alone with her elderly grandmother and her blind grandfather. As a result, the girl's mother is facing a criminal case. She stands accused of leaving a minor in danger in the care of the elderly. She also faces investigation from childcare services, who will also be asking why Karla was left alone with her vulnerable relatives.
The journey took place in February when temperatures average negative 26 degrees Celsius. Russian reports on social media suggest the forest may have been as cold as negative 34 degrees Celsius. The journey was only recently confirmed by authorities.
But though she was suffering from the effects of extreme cold, the child reportedly suffered no life-threatening effects. Last year, a three-year-old boy survived alone for three days in a remote forest in the same region.

A）女孩的祖父是盲人，原文未提及“照顾祖父”是女孩的目的；

D）森林中存在熊和狼的威胁，但女孩并非为了“逃离熊的威胁”而行动。 涉及知识点：事实细节题的目的类信息抓取、动词短语（seek help for 为……求助）的理解。

questions.script:
W: I've made a new friend recently. Her name is Susan and she's from South Africa.
M: How did you meet her?
W: We met over WeChat. She has very cool photos on her social media. The photos of her hometown look amazing.
M: What's her hometown called?
W: It's called Cape Town. It's in the southwest of South Africa. She says it's very green and windy. The city was built by European settlers. And there's a big mountain that overlooks the city. The mountain is called Table Mountain because it's flat at the top.
M: That sounds interesting. What are the people there like?
W: Well, Susan says South Africa is very mixed. There are black people and white people and Indian people. Susan is white. She says her ancestors were from Britain. Many languages are spoken in South Africa, but she only speaks English.
M: Didn't South Africa host the Football World Cup a few years ago? They must play football a lot then, right?
W: I think they play football, but it's not as popular as rugby.
M: Rugby? What's rugby?
W: Rugby is a sport with two teams and the players carry the ball in their arms and throw it at each other. The ball is not round and the players push each other. I don't really understand the rules. I think it's very complicated.
M: That sounds like a very strange sport indeed. Is it only South Africa that plays it?
W: No, it's also popular in Britain and in other former British colonies like Australia and New Zealand.

questions.script:
The golden rule is a moral principle which states that you should treat others the way you want to be treated yourself. For example, if you want people to treat you with respect, you should treat them with respect.
Different people tend to be exposed to different forms of the golden rule, based on factors such as the religion in their society.
However, all forms of the golden rule revolve around the same concept. Namely, they help you treat others better, by using the way you yourself would want to be treated as a guide of how to behave.
A notable criticism of the golden rule is that its application can lead to undesirable outcomes, when it conflicts with laws and ethical principles.
For example, if someone breaks the law, the golden rule would suggest that we should let them go, because we would not want to be punished ourselves.
However, this issue with the golden rule can be dealt with in a general manner, by viewing this principle as one of several principles that we use to guide our behavior as individuals and as a society.
Specifically, in the example described above, most individuals and societies choose to place laws and ethical principles above the golden rule. This means that they strive to implement the golden rule whenever possible, as long as it doesn't clash with a more important concept.

questions.script:
Today, many large corporations stress the importance of diversity on their websites, but current statistics show that the typical manager in America still tends to be white and male. Obviously, the desire to bring about diversity has not translated into corporate reality.
Why useless? A team of researchers from the University of Basel published their new study about people's attitudes towards diversity at work. They found that people have a wide range of opinions concerning diversity. On the one hand, many see value in diversity, which can contribute a variety of perspectives, encourage new ideas, and generate innovative solutions. On the other hand, they assume that it might be difficult to work with someone who has completely different views, speaks a different language, or has a different style of work.
The actual value they attribute to diversity depends on the decision-making perspective. Doubts about the practicability of diversity have a greater weight if a person is directly affected. In other words, when a person's own work group is involved, they tend to prefer team members who are similar to themselves. But when people make decisions for others, they typically put together a more diverse team. These findings could help organizations become more diverse. Companies need to pay attention to who makes hiring and team decisions.
These decisions should not only be made by those directly affected. People who are not directly involved in the group's daily work should also take part.

questions.script:
Today, many large corporations stress the importance of diversity on their websites, but current statistics show that the typical manager in America still tends to be white and male. Obviously, the desire to bring about diversity has not translated into corporate reality.
Why useless? A team of researchers from the University of Basel published their new study about people's attitudes towards diversity at work. They found that people have a wide range of opinions concerning diversity. On the one hand, many see value in diversity, which can contribute a variety of perspectives, encourage new ideas, and generate innovative solutions. On the other hand, they assume that it might be difficult to work with someone who has completely different views, speaks a different language, or has a different style of work.

questions.script:
Communication can essentially be divided into two categories: the written and the spoken.
How the balance is struck between these two forms of communication—the point at which one needs to be exchanged for another—really depends on individual cultures.
Understanding when it's appropriate to exchange one form for another can be a major key to success in international business.
Many cultures place a much greater value on the spoken word than the American working culture does.
In parts of the Middle East, you'll find spoken word agreements are seen as seriously binding. A person's word is linked to their honor, so verbal agreements are seen as important, whereas written contracts are taken as memos of understanding.
Western working culture tends to place a high value on the written word, and this reaches its highest level of intensity when it comes to contracts. In the US, France and Germany, written contracts tend to be seen as something that must be strictly carried out.
By contrast, other cultures may not see written contracts as quite so binding. It can prove a challenge to Western businesses if your business partner wants to renegotiate terms that you thought were already agreed on.
For example, a Japanese firm may have signed a contract, but they may not feel bound by every detail of it—particularly if circumstances later change.
Such differences in value that different working cultures place on the written word tend to cause many problems when it comes to business relationships.

questions.expl: 定位：由题干中的“reading its description”和“ideal”定位到文章A段：“理论上，这份工作对我来说似乎很完美：这个职位与我的学位完全相符，工作职责与我的兴趣相符，而且办公室有一个储备充足的厨房，可以满足我对零食的各种需求。” 精析：本题为细节归纳题。题干中的“reading its description”对应定位段中的“On paper”（字面意义上；理论上，即通过职位描述），“the author found the job offered ideal”对应“the job seemed perfect for me”，题干是对定位段的归纳总结，语义一致。 涉及知识点：细节题的关键词定位（On paper = reading its description；perfect = ideal）、归纳总结能力。

questions.stem: 40. Job applicants are advised to make a written list of their likes and dislikes in their previous employment.
questions.expl: 定位：由题干中的“make a written list”“likes and dislikes”和“previous employment”定位到文章F段第一、二句：“首先写下你不喜欢前任雇主的地方，以及你真正看重的部分。这里没有错误的答案——所以从大事到小细节，把它们都写在你的清单上。” 精析：本题为细节归纳题。题干中的“make a written list”对应“write them all down on your list”，“likes and dislikes”对应“the parts you really valued”（喜欢的部分）和“the things you didn't like”（不喜欢的部分），“previous employment”对应“previous employers”，题干是对定位句的概括归纳，语义一致。 涉及知识点：细节题的关键词定位（written list = write down on your list；likes and dislikes = valued + didn't like）、概括归纳能力。

questions.stem: 41. At the end of an interview, a job applicant should seize the opportunity to get answers to their urgent
questions.expl: 定位：由题干中的“At the end of an interview”“opportunity”和“urgent questions”定位到文章K段第二、三句：“你知道在面试结束时，招聘负责人问你有没有什么问题，你只是张着嘴茫然地盯着桌子对面吗？这是一个很好的机会，你可以大声说出自己的想法，让招聘负责人回答你迫切想了解的企业文化的问题！” 精析：本题为细节归纳题。题干中的“At the end of an interview”对应“at the end of a job interview”，“the opportunity to get answers to their urgent questions”对应“the perfect opportunity”和“get your burning company culture questions answered”（“burning”与“urgent”同义），题干是对定位句的概括归纳，语义一致。 涉及知识点：细节题的同义替换（urgent = burning；get answers = get... answered）、概括归纳能力。

questions.stem: 42. To begin with, job applicants should be clear what they expect from their future employer.
questions.expl: 定位：由题干中的“be clear”和“what they expect”定位到文章E段第三句：“所以，在你确定自己和某家公司是否合拍之前，先明确你到底想从雇主那里得到什么，这一点很重要。” 精析：本题为细节归纳题。题干中的“be clear”对应定位句中的“have a solid handle on”（掌握；明确），“what they expect from their future employer”对应“what exactly you want from your employer”，题干是对定位句的归纳总结，语义一致。 涉及知识点：细节题的同义替换（be clear = have a solid handle on；expect = want）、归纳总结能力。

questions.stem: 43. Job applicants should read with a critical eye what is written about a company on the website.
questions.expl: 【答案】I。 【解析】定位 I 段第二句。作者提醒求职者对网站评论持保留态度，因为不少评论来自愤愤不平的员工。read with a critical eye 是 take ... with a grain of salt 的同义改写，故选 I。

questions.stem: 44. Job satisfaction has a lot to do with company culture.
questions.expl: 定位：由题干中的“Job satisfaction”和“company culture”定位到文章C段最后一句：“公司文化会对你的工作感受产生很大的影响，所以你要确保你是跟真正感兴趣的公司签了聘用函。” 精析：本题为细节辨认题。题干中的“Job satisfaction”对应定位句中的“how you feel about your work”（工作感受即工作满意度），“has a lot to do with”对应“have a big impact on”（对……有重大影响），“company culture”在定位句中直接出现，题干与定位句语义一致。 涉及知识点：细节题的同义替换（Job satisfaction = how you feel about your work；has a lot to do with = have a big impact on）、细节辨认能力。

questions.stem: 45. A chat with an insider of a company can give job applicants very useful information when they prepare for an interview.
questions.expl: 定位：由题干中的“A chat”“an insider of a company”和“useful information”定位到文章J段第二、三句：“通过Linkedln或电子邮件给该公司的在职员工或离职员工发一条简短的信息，询问他们是否愿意和你就该公司的总体情况进行简短的交谈。如果你的聊天请求得到了同意，你将会带着一些非常强大和有用的信息进入面试！” 精析：本题为细节辨认题。题干中的“A chat”在定位句中直接出现，“an insider of a company”对应“a current or previous company employee”（在职或离职员工即公司内部人士），“very useful information”对应“pretty powerful and helpful information”，题干是对定位句的总结，语义一致。 涉及知识点：细节题的关键词定位（insider = current or previous employee；useful = powerful and helpful）、总结能力。

questions.stem: 46. What does the author say about students enrolled in online classes?

options.A: They can access course materials easily.
options.B: They are unmotivated to learn.
options.C: They can learn at their own pace.
options.D: They rarely fulfil the course requirements.

questions.expl:
详解： 定位：由题干中的“students enrolled in online classes”定位到文章第二、三段。 精析：本题为细节辨认题。第三段明确提到“First of all, students lack the desire to learn, and they simply complete their assignments to receive credit for a passing grade rather than genuinely engage with the course material”，其中“lack the desire to learn”与选项B中的“unmotivated to learn”为同义替换，直接说明在线课程学生缺乏学习动力，仅为及格而完成作业，并非真正参与学习。 干扰项分析：
A）原文未提及“学生可轻松获取课程材料”，仅提到课程材料未被学生深入参与；
C）“按自己的节奏学习”是在线课程的宣传卖点，并非作者对学生的观察结论；
D）原文提到学生“完成作业以获得及格分数”，并非“很少达到课程要求”。 涉及知识点：细节题的定位与同义替换（lack the desire to learn = unmotivated to learn）、区分宣传卖点与作者实际观察。

questions.stem: 47. What does the author think of online course assignments?

options.A: They are made convenient to mark.
options.B: They are meant to facilitate interaction.
options.C: They are based on easily accessible material.
options.D: They are given to accommodate students’needs.

questions.expl:
详解： 定位：由题干中的“online course assignments”定位到文章第四段。 精析：本题为细节辨认题。第四段第二句明确提到“They are not designed for students to interact with the material in depth but designed to be graded easily to accommodate such a large number of students”，其中“graded easily”与选项A中的“convenient to mark”为同义替换，直接说明在线课程作业设计的目的是便于评分，以适应大量学生的情况，而非让学生深入学习。 干扰项分析：
B）与原文“并非为了让学生深入互动”相悖；
C）原文未提及作业“基于易于获取的材料”；
D）原文提到作业设计是为了“容纳大量学生”，而非“满足学生需求”。 涉及知识点：细节题的定位与同义替换（graded easily = convenient to mark）、转折关系信息抓取（not... but... 并非……而是……）。

questions.stem: 48. What does the author say is one disadvantage of online classes?

options.A: They are frequently scheduled at irregular times.
options.B: They make professors’offices much less accessible.
options.C: They tend to increase professors’burden of responding to students’emails.
options.D: They provide little chance for students to build relationships with each other. 2022 年 6 月英语四级真题 第一套 页码 8

questions.expl:
详解： 定位：由题干中的“one disadvantage of online classes”定位到文章第五段第一句。 精析：本题为细节辨认题。第五段指出在线课程最大的缺点是“the absence of face-to-face interaction between the teacher and their students”，第六段进一步补充“There is also little interaction amongst students. It can be harder for students to create study groups and form relationships with their peers”，即学生之间互动少，难以建立关系，选项D是对该内容的同义表述。 干扰项分析：
A）原文提到直播课程“通常安排在正午”，并非“不定期时间”；
B）原文提到学生可能不便参加教授办公时间，并非“教授办公室更难进入”；
C）原文提到师生互动多通过电子邮件，“缺少人情味”，但未提及“增加教授回复邮件的负担”。 涉及知识点：细节题的段落间信息整合（教师与学生互动少+学生之间互动少）、同义替换（little interaction amongst students = little chance to build relationships）。

questions.stem: 49. What problem may arise if classes go online?

options.A: More students may find it easy to be absent from them.
options.B: Teachers will worry about poor internet connections.
options.C: Some students may have difficulty attending them.
options.D: Schools with limited resources will be at a disadvantage.

questions.expl:
详解： 定位：由题干中的“classes go online”和题文同序原则定位到文章第七段。 精析：本题为推理判断题。第七段提到“Online classes also require either a computer or laptop and a reliable internet connection. Not all students have access to these types of resources, whether it is for financial or other reasons, and some students can be put at a disadvantage”，即在线课程需要电脑和稳定网络，而部分学生因经济或其他原因无法获得这些资源，由此可推断这些学生可能难以参加在线课程，选项C正确。 干扰项分析：
A）原文未提及“学生更容易逃课”；
B）原文未提到“教师担心网络连接问题”；
D）原文强调“学生因缺乏资源处于劣势”，并非“资源有限的学校处于劣势”。 涉及知识点：推理判断题的因果关系推理（需要资源→部分学生无资源→难以参加）、细节定位与语义转换。

questions.stem: 50. What does the author think constitutes a key part of genuine education?

options.A: Acquisition of useful knowledge.
options.B: Training of real-life skills on campus.
options.C: Development of students’personalities.
options.D: Cultivation of analytical thinking ability.

questions.expl:
详解： 定位：由题干中的“genuine education”定位到文章最后一段第二句。 精析：本题为推理判断题。最后一段第二句提到“they fail to provide a genuine education with an emphasis on convenience rather than critical thinking”，即在线课程强调便利性而非批判性思维，未能提供真正的教育，由此可推断“批判性思维（分析思维能力）的培养”是真正教育的核心部分，选项D正确。 干扰项分析：
A）“获取有用知识”、
B）“校园内培训现实生活技能”、
C）“学生个性发展”均未在原文中被提及为真正教育的核心要素。 涉及知识点：推理判断题的反向推理（缺乏批判性思维→真正教育需包含批判性思维）、同义替换（critical thinking = analytical thinking ability）。

questions.stem: 51. What does the author think open debate can do?

options.A: Help the public to better understand science.
options.B: Clear up confusion in the scientific community.
options.C: Settle disputes between universities and government agencies.
options.D: Prevent information from being used incorrectly by the public.

questions.expl:
详解： 定位：由题干中的“open debate”定位到文章第一段第四句。 精析：本题为细节辨认题。第一段第四句提到“yet, open debate can also promote communication between the scientific community and the public”，且后文补充“helps the public observe the process of scientific discourse more clearly”，即公开辩论能促进科学界与公众的沟通，帮助公众更清晰地了解科学论述过程，选项A是对该内容的同义概括。 干扰项分析：
B）原文提到公开辩论可能“导致公众混乱”，并非“消除科学界的混乱”；
C）原文提到辩论“走出大学和政府机构大厅”，并非“解决大学与政府机构的纠纷”；
D）原文提到公开辩论“存在信息被误用的潜在风险”，并非“防止公众误用信息”。 涉及知识点：细节题的定位与概括（promote communication + observe scientific discourse more clearly = better understand science）、转折关系信息抓取（yet 引导的转折）。

questions.stem: 52. Why did a recent debate published in The New York Times arouse concerns among experts?

options.A: It might hinder the progress in medical research.
options.B: It might breed public distrust in modem medicine.
options.C: It might add to the difficulty of getting research funds.
options.D: It might prevent medical scientists reaching consensus.、

questions.expl:
It might breed public distrust in modern medicine. 详解： 定位：由题干中的“The New York Times”和“arouse concerns”定位到文章第二段。 精析：本题为推理判断题。第二段第三句提到“some experts worried that such public speculation might lead people to believe that disagreement about the details meant a lack of adequate scientific consensus over the safety and efficiency of modern-day medicine”，即专家担心公众会将细节分歧误解为现代医学在安全性和有效性上缺乏科学共识，由此可推断这会引发公众对现代医学的不信任，选项B正确。 干扰项分析：
A）原文未提及“阻碍医学研究进展”；
C）原文未涉及“研究资金困难”；
D）原文提到专家担心公众误解“缺乏共识”，并非“阻碍医学科学家达成共识”。 涉及知识点：推理判断题的因果关系推理（公众误解→不信任）、语义转换（lack of scientific consensus → distrust）。

questions.stem: 53. Why does the author say some experts’anxiety seems misplaced?

options.A: Debating scientific issues at a conference is now old-fashioned.
options.B: Diverse topics can be debated by both scientists and the public.
options.C: Debates about science are accessible to the public anyway.
options.D: Scientists can voice their opinions whatever way they like.

questions.expl:
详解： 定位：由题干中的“some experts’anxiety seems misplaced”定位到文章第三段。 精析：本题为细节辨认题。第三段首句指出专家的焦虑“放错了地方”，末句进一步解释“These days, the public can access debates about science regardless of where they take place”，即如今公众无论在何处都能接触到科学辩论，因此专家担心“公开辩论导致误解”是多余的，选项C正确。 干扰项分析：
A）原文提到“会议辩论的日子一去不复返”，但这并非专家焦虑放错地方的原因；
B）原文未提及“科学家和公众可讨论多种话题”；
D）原文未提到“科学家可随意表达观点”。 涉及知识点：细节题的因果关系定位（专家焦虑多余的原因→公众可接触科学辩论）、同义替换（access = accessible）。

questions.stem: 54. What does the author suggest scientists do about public debate?

options.A: Have more discussions about it.
options.B: Embrace it with open arms.
options.C: Formulate new rules for it.
options.D: Restrain it to a rational degree.

questions.expl:
Embrace it with open arms. 详解： 定位：由题干中的“scientists”“public debate”和题文同序原则定位到文章第四段首句。 精析：本题为推理判断题。第四段首句提到“but rather than avoiding such conversations, let the debates be transparent and vigorous, wherever they are held”，即科学家不应回避公开辩论，而应让辩论透明、激烈，无论在何处举行，由此可推断作者建议科学家“欣然接受”公开辩论，选项B正确。 干扰项分析：
A）原文未建议“多讨论公开辩论本身”；
C）原文提到公开辩论“似乎没有太多限制或规则”，但未建议“制定新规则”；
D）原文未提及“将辩论限制在合理程度”。 涉及知识点：推理判断题的建议类信息抓取（rather than avoiding → embrace）、语义转换。

questions.stem: 55. What does the author say about science in the last paragraph?

options.A: It is transmitted through textbooks.
options.B: It is what proves valid and true to life.
options.C: It is a dynamic and self-improving process.
options.D: It is a collection of facts and established rules.

questions.expl:
It is a dynamic and self-improving process. 详解： 定位：由题干中的“the last paragraph”定位到文章最后一段。 精析：本题为推理判断题。最后一段第二句提到“science is an honorably self-correcting process”，即科学是一个正大光明的自我纠正过程，“自我纠正”意味着动态发展、不断完善，选项C是对该内容的同义概括。 干扰项分析：
A）原文提到需摒弃“科学是教科书中固定事实”的观点，并非“科学通过教材传播”；
B）原文提到科学辩论应“真实反映生活”，并非“科学是有效且真实的”；
D）与原文“科学不是固定事实的集合”相悖。 涉及知识点：推理判断题的语义概括（self-correcting process = dynamic and self-improving process）、反向信息排除（摒弃错误观点→排除D选项）。
